notes: Britain and its colonies form one realm (Great Britain, before the 1801 union).
Louisiana was Spanish from 1762 to 1800; Quebec British from 1763.
Split 'central Asian khanates' into Khiva, Bukhara, Kokand and the Kazakh juzes.
Sardinia island belonged to the Kingdom of Sardinia (Savoy).
Filled unclaimed land with peoples and cultures from neighbouring maps.
Named the remaining unclaimed regions after their regional peoples.
The Electorate of Hanover was labelled Mecklenburg-Strelitz; Mecklenburg-Strelitz is now drawn in the east of Mecklenburg, as on the 1815 map.
Silesia was drawn as "Slavic tribes"; it was Prussian from 1742. Bavaria (with the Palatinate) has its own outline; the rest of southern and western Germany is the Holy Roman Empire's smaller states.
"Malaya" is a British-era name; the peninsula and its neighbours were Malay sultanates.
The Canary Islands were conquered by Castile by 1496; the Guanche territory is Castilian/Spanish here.
Hong Kong was part of Qing China until 1841; it no longer shows as a separate territory.
There was no Senegal before the French colony; the area was held by the Wolof and Fula kingdoms.
The Kingdom of Benin and the Niger delta were labelled "Sotho", a people of southern Africa; the land west of it was labelled "Africa".
Zanzibar was not a separate sultanate until 1856; the Swahili coast was under Omani overlordship.
The Austronesian peoples of Taiwan and the islands were coloured as the Habsburg Monarchy.
The Dutch left Taiwan in 1662 and the Qing took the west of the island in 1683.
North Africa is named for its rulers of the time.
Peoples and archaeological cultures are shown only while they existed.
Names respelled.
Colonies are shown as colonies, under the power that held them at this date, and only where it held them (lines approximate).
